chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about taking out the meat of the sacrificial animals from Mina, so he said: 'We used to say: Do not take anything out of it due to the people's need for it. But as for today, since the people have become numerous, there is no problem with taking it out.'

key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / it is permissible
key_terms.لِحَاجَةِ النَّاسِ إِلَيْهِ: Due to the people's need for it

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on taking sacrificial meat out of Mina after Eid al-Adha?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) illustrates the principle of *al-taghayyur bi-taghayyur al-zaman* (change of ruling with the change of time), where the prohibition against removing meat from Mina was lifted due to demographic shifts and reduced scarcity. It highlights the dynamic nature of Shia fiqh, showing how practical necessities (*hajah*) and public welfare (*maslahah*) can modify specific prohibitions without altering the core ritual. This ruling is particularly significant for understanding the flexibility of Hajj regulations in response to changing social conditions.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about taking the meat of the slaughtered animal out from Mina. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘We<sup>asws</sup> were saying: ‘Do not take anything out (from Mina) due to the needs of the people for it’. But, as for today, so the people have become numerous, therefore there is no problem with taking it out (from Mina)’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about taking out from Mina’ the meat of the offering animals.
He (the Imam) said, ‘We would say that it must not be taken out of Mina’ because people needed. Today, however, the number of people has increased, thus it is not harmful to take out of MinaY”
